transcript.content: Hello, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because it’s gotten pretty bad at work. I’m a barber, and I’ll do almost anything to avoid using the straight razor now—switch clients, say the blade’s missing, even hide it in the drawer. And if I can’t get out of it, I’m shaking through the whole shave.
When you have to use the straight razor, are you mainly afraid that you might accidentally cut or seriously hurt the client?

Yeah. I mean, I know it’s just a tool, and I was trained to use it. I can use clippers all day without thinking about it. But when that straight razor is open at my station, it feels like I’m about to hurt the client—or cut myself badly.
Outside of using the straight razor, do you find yourself worrying a lot about many other parts of life?
Not really, no. I mean, I worry about normal stuff sometimes, but it’s not like my mind is always jumping to a bunch of different things. It’s mainly this razor situation that gets to me.
When the fear about the straight razor comes up, do you feel like you have to do any repeated ritual or checking to make the anxiety go down?

I don’t think so. I mean, I might put the razor away or avoid picking it up, but I’m not doing a ritual or checking over and over to make it feel better. It’s more like I just want to get away from it.
